👨‍🎓 Learner: Thomas Shelby (423 Total Speech Turns)
Impact of Speech Rate on ASR ⚠️
Tracking Match Confidence and extreme speech rate across 4 sessions:
Session 1 Confidence: 0.801 | Moderate rate: 3.56 w/s | 0.11 Hesitations
Session 2 (Peak Quality) Confidence: 0.845 | Rate: 3.59 w/s | 0.04 Hesitations
Session 3 Confidence: 0.608 | Accelerated rate: 5.48 w/s ⚠️ | 0.22 Hesitations
Session 4 Confidence: 0.592 | Highly accelerated rate: 5.85 w/s | 0.09 Hesitations
Critical Insight for Research Question #7: Thomas Shelby's case demonstrates that a sharp surge in speech rate (from 3.5 words/sec to ~5.8 words/sec, >350 WPM) causes coarticulation, syllable dropping, and ASR transcription errors, explaining why Speech_Rate is the primary acoustic predictor in our model!

🏆 Performance Comparison Across 5 Algorithms (Task A: Binary Classification)
5-Fold Stratified Cross-Validation on 732 Verified Rows with 9 Multimodal Features:
XGBoost Classifier 🥇 92.49% (F1: 94.21%)
Random Forest (100 Trees) 🥈 91.39% (F1: 93.35%)
Logistic Regression 🥉 91.26% (F1: 93.02%)
Neural Network (MLP: 16x8) 91.12% (F1: 93.21%)
Support Vector Machine (SVM - RBF) 90.30% (F1: 92.24%)
💡 Key Scientific Finding: Following the synchronization of 732 homogeneous, noise-free samples (Clean Corpus), XGBoost surges to 92.49% accuracy and a 94.21% F1-Score! Tree-based and ensemble models effectively leverage the complexity of multimodal features when sample size is sufficient.

🗣️ Learner Error & Disfluency Preservation (Guidelines p. 7)
Evaluating formula: Learner Error Preservation Rate vs. LLM tendency to normalize and smooth imperfect speech:
Acoustic Transcript (Whisper) 25.4% (15 of 59 turns)
Textual Transcript (ChatGPT) 3.4% (2 of 59 turns)
💡 Definitive Answer to Research Question #2:
While ChatGPT automatically deleted or normalized virtually all learner hesitations and stutters (96.6% erased), the acoustic Whisper model preserved natural conversational fillers ("um", "uh", repetitions, self-repairs) at a rate 7.5x higher! 7.5x!

💡 Multimodal Feature Importance (XGBoost Feature Importance)
Ranking of 9 multimodal features (acoustic & linguistic) predicting whether a speech turn requires human correction (based on 732 verified samples):
1. Match_Confidence (Lexical alignment & divergence between Whisper and ChatGPT) 65.34%
2. Different_Words (Substituted words between ASR systems) 7.64%
3. Speech_Rate (Speech pacing in words per second) 6.64%
4. Silence_Before_Turn (Pause duration before speech turn starts) 4.74%
5. Missing_Words (Omitted or dropped words during articulation) 4.19%
6. Hesitations_Count (Fillers "um", "uh", repetitions, and self-repairs) 4.09%
7. Speech_Volume (Acoustic signal energy in RMS dB) 3.68%
8. Noise_Level (Background noise to signal ratio - SNR) 3.67%
9. Has_Overlap (Vocal overlap between speakers) 0.01%
